title: A Game-Theoretic Negotiation Framework for Cross-Cultural Consensus in LLMs
benchmark_measurement: The framework evaluates the ability of culturally-aligned LLM agents (representing groups including religious-cultural clusters like 'African-Islamic' and 'Confucian') to negotiate and reach a fair, balanced consensus on contentious topics. One of the six explicit topic categories for negotiation is 'Religion and Secularism', which examines the relationship between religious beliefs and secular governance.
religious_groups: Christianity (as Orthodox Europe, Catholic Europe, Protestant Europe)
findings: In a case study negotiation between an 'African-Islamic' agent and an 'English-Speaking' agent, the proposed game-theoretic method resulted in a balanced consensus, with both agents converging on the shared value of 'Respect Sovereignty.' This contrasts with baseline debate methods where the minority (African-Islamic) perspective tended to shift towards the majority WEIRD viewpoint. Additionally, fine-tuning with negotiation data caused agents, including the African-Islamic agent, to shift towards more 'traditional' values on the Inglehart-Welzel Cultural Map.
